component.name: Ultron
component.summary: Flash and unbrick Qualcomm EDL devices

description.p: Ultron is a graphical flashing and unbricking tool for Qualcomm devices in Emergency Download (EDL / 9008) mode. It uploads the device's signed Firehose programmer over the Sahara protocol and flashes images using qdl-compatible rawprogram/patch XML layouts.

The protocol implementation is a port of the well-tested open-source qdl tool, cross-checked against the edl and edl-ng projects. Device access is detected live over hot-plug; every protocol exchange is shown in the built-in console.
Ultron's architecture is modular: MediaTek (BROM) and Samsung (Odin) protocol modules are planned on top of the same plugin interface.

Hardening release from a five-agent code audit: worker threads are joined at shutdown, cancelling the connect probe no longer wedges the UI, partition reads reject truncated data and verify the GPT entry CRC, out-of-range UFS provisioning values are rejected instead of aborting, queued writes can no longer survive a disconnect or land on another device/LUN, VIP digest tables regenerate cleanly into the same folder, file choosers are modal, and several small leaks and doc drifts were fixed.

Huawei UPDATE.APP support: flash an entire Huawei firmware package to a Qualcomm EDL device — entries are matched to the loaded GPT partitions by name, Android sparse images are converted to raw automatically (streamed from the container where possible), and every image write is verified with the device-side SHA-256.

Verification and recovery release: per-partition Erase, automatic write verification (device SHA-256 vs local image), a RAM dump page for crash-dump (900e) devices, storage-type fallback plus a Skip-storage-init switch, multi-device targeting by bus/device or serial, VIP digest-table support, and qdl's two-pass UFS provisioning with an explicit OTP-lock gate.

Unified single-page workflow: connect, upload the firehose loader (skipped automatically when a programmer is already running), browse the device partition table per LUN, back partitions up (Read) or flash images to them (Write) with a queued batch and a single destructive confirmation. rawprogram/patch XML support retained.

Initial release: Qualcomm EDL flashing with full qdl parity (Sahara programmer upload, Firehose configure/program/erase/patch, set-bootable, reset), device hot-plug detection, chip identity probe, and a live protocol console.
